speaker: Sheldon
text: No, I said there. What's the difference? In the winter, that seat is close enough to the radiator to remain warm and yet not so close as to cause perspiration. In the summer, it's directly in the path of a cross breeze created by opening windows there and there. It faces the television at an angle that is neither direct, thus discouraging conversation, nor so far wide as to create a parallax distortion.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I could go on, but I think I've made my point.

speaker: Penny
text: What's the difference? Do you want me to move?

speaker: Leonard
text: Here we go. Well, sit somewhere else.

speaker: Leonard
text: We don't have a lot of company over.

speaker: Sheldon
text: That's not true. Kuther, Polly, and Wolowitz come over all the time. Tuesday night, we played Klingon Boggle until one in the morning. I resent you saying we don't have company. That is a negative social implication.

speaker: Leonard
text: I'm sorry. I said I'm sorry.

speaker: Leonard
text: Yeah, it's like regular Boggle, but in Klingon.
